## MACHINE SPEC (mechanical intent — compile the coordination)
This section is AUTHORITATIVE intent authored by the mechanical engineer.
Synthesize the signals, waits, exits, and cross-station handshakes that
realize it. EVERY wait you create must have an exit for every partner
failure mode listed here PLUS a timeout — no exitless waits.

### Device purposes
- Escapement_Finger_1: Escapement stop at the end of the track — extends to hold back the queued parts once a part is captured in the shuttle dead nest.
- Escapement_Finger_2: Second escapement stop at the end of the track, working with finger 1 to release one mid-base at a time into the shuttle nest.
- Escapement_Shuttle: MXS slide below the track carrying the dead nest — sits in line with the track to receive a part, then carries it away from the track to the pick position.
- Shuttle_Gripper: Holds the mid-base in the shuttle dead nest while the shuttle carries it out to pick, releases after the PnP gripper has the part.
- Nest_Part_Present: Confirms a mid-base has fed into the shuttle dead nest before the shuttle gripper closes.
- X_Axis: Servo traverse of the pick-and-place between the pick position over the shuttle and the place position at the dial.
- Vertical_Slide: MXS slide, 150 mm stroke, raising and lowering the PnP gripper at pick and at the dial; retract sensor only, about 1 second to extend.
- PNP_Gripper: Grips the mid-base for the transfer from the shuttle nest to the dial; no sensors, 250 ms grip/release timer.

## GENERATION SCOPE (contract — what this build covers vs not)
THIS BUILD GENERATES: station sequence logic; servo motion commands; device commands & verification; state transitions; basic sequence faults/retries needed for the sequence.
NOT IN THIS BUILD (machine-level extras deferred until the station joins a machine): machine-level part tracking; upstream/downstream coordination beyond defined IO; overall machine initialization; machine-wide fault manager; production/OEE logic; supervisor sequencing outside this station.
Scope law: NEVER ask about, flag, or apologize for NOT-IN-THIS-BUILD items.
Where the sequence touches one (e.g. a partner/supervisor signal outside the
defined IO), stub it quietly per the SDC standalone pattern (*Replace rung
comment) and move on — that is your own decision, not a question. A
standalone sequence terminates cleanly in "Sequence Complete / Ready for
next command".
The station-level template pieces ALWAYS emit regardless of scope: init
block, lockout, R01 inputs, station part-tracking block, alarms — the full
station file, never a reduced one.
